info.title: AtlasFetch
info.description:
Send a coordinate; get back the country, region and municipality that contain it,
plus matches from your own uploaded boundary sets — in one call. Optionally, the
nearest street and house number, worldwide (per-country detail at /streets/coverage).

**When to use it:** reverse geocoding to administrative areas, geofencing against your
own polygons, jurisdiction and region checks, enriching location data with region codes.

**When not to:** forward geocoding (address to coordinate) or place search, a
guaranteed house number (OpenStreetMap maps them unevenly), routing or map tiles,
retrieving boundary or street geometry, many coordinates in one request, or
enter/exit event tracking.

A fuller reference for automated clients is at https://atlasfetch.xyz/llms.txt

Reference boundaries and streets derive from OpenStreetMap under the ODbL; attribution and
share-alike obligations pass through to you. Looked-up coordinates are not stored.

get.summary: Resolve a coordinate to the boundaries that contain it
get.description:
Point-in-polygon lookup. Returns the administrative boundaries containing the point
and any matches from the account's own boundary sets.

Add `street` to `base` for the nearest street: three answers, within 5 m, within
20 m and unlimited, each a house number and street, or a street alone, with its
distance. Worldwide: 216 countries (`GET /streets/coverage`). `null` only outside them,
for example at sea.

One request is one billed lookup, however many layers, sets or grid codes it touches.
Metering happens before matching, so a call that matches nothing still bills.

`errors[]` is present on every response. A set that cannot be queried is skipped and
reported there with HTTP 200 — it does not fail the request.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Comma-separated reference layers to resolve: `country`, `region`, `municipal`, `street`. Defaults to the first three; `street` is opt-in.

parameters.name: set
parameters.description: Comma-separated names of your own boundary sets to match against. Defaults to none.

parameters.name: encode
parameters.description: Comma-separated grid encodings to express the point in: `h3`, `pluscode`. Output only — neither is accepted as a location. Not metered.

parameters.name: h3res
parameters.description: H3 resolution, 0-15. r9 is roughly 400 m across.

parameters.name: pluslen
parameters.description: Plus Code length. 9 is not a valid Plus Code length.

200.description: The point resolved. Check `errors[]` for per-set problems.

X-Lookups-Remaining.description: Lookups left in the current billing period.

400.description: Invalid parameters — including a Plus Code or H3 index sent as the location, which is refused on purpose. Not billed.

401.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key.

402.description: Monthly lookup allowance exhausted. Retry after the period resets.

429.description: Per-key rate limit exceeded. Honour Retry-After. Not billed.

post.description:
A new set is created with `available: false` and no key grants, so it matches nothing
until both are changed.

**A client holding only an API key cannot finish this on its own.** Grants are addressed
by API key *id*, and the only endpoint that lists key ids requires a browser session, so
the grant step happens in the dashboard at https://atlasfetch.xyz/dashboard

name.description: 1-32 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter or digit.

201.description: The set was created — unavailable and granted to no key.

400.description: The name does not match the allowed pattern.

401.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key.

403.description: The plan's set cap was reached.

409.description: A set of that name already exists.

schema.description: 1-32 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter or digit.

patch.summary: Toggle availability, grant or revoke keys
patch.description: A set is only queryable when `available` is true **and** the calling key is granted it.

available.description: The account-wide master switch for this set.

200.description: The updated set, in the same shape as the list.

401.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key.

404.description: No such set on this account, or a key id in grant/revoke is not one of its keys.

post.summary: Add a polygon to a set
post.description:
Stores one polygon in an existing set. Each call creates a new boundary; the same name twice
stores two.

Plan caps apply to vertices per polygon (every ring position counts, including the closing
one), properties per boundary, and boundaries per set. At the boundaries-per-set cap the
Public plan — the shared demo key — silently deletes the oldest boundary to make room; every
other plan refuses with 403.

set.description: The existing set to add it to.

name.description: Returned when a looked-up point falls inside it.

201.description: The boundary was stored. Geometry is not echoed back.

400.description: Not a valid GeoJSON Polygon (wrong type, unclosed or short ring, out-of-range or non-numeric positions, self-intersection), a bad name, or a property of the wrong type or length.

401.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key.

403.description: A plan cap was hit: too many vertices, too many properties, a property the Public plan does not allow, or a full set on a plan that refuses rather than evicts.

404.description: No such set on this account.

get.summary: Countries that answer the street layer
get.description:
The countries that answer `base=street` — 216, every country with an ISO code —
with their OpenStreetMap snapshot and road and address counts. Outside them `street`
is null. `addresses` is the number of mapped addresses: roads are well mapped almost
everywhere, house numbers vary widely by country, and this is how to judge one.

snapshotDate.description: The OpenStreetMap snapshot the data came from.

addresses.description: Mapped addresses — the ceiling on how often a house number can come back.

post.summary: Route between two or more coordinates
post.description:
A route from the first location to the last, via any between. Costs **10 lookups** from
the monthly allowance, whatever it asks for. Durations are free-flow estimates with no
traffic. Optional: turn-by-turn steps, the route line, up to 2 alternatives (2 locations
only), avoid zones taken from your own boundary sets, and exposure: how far the route
runs inside the zones of other sets. A zone containing one of the locations is not
avoided for that route, and `avoid.skipped` says so. Coordinates go in the body,
never the URL, and are not stored.

400.description: `code` invalid_request, too_far or avoid_too_complex. Not billed.

401.description: Missing, malformed or revoked API key.

403.description: `code` plan_feature (a mode or cap above the plan) or avoid_set_unavailable. Not billed.

422.description: `code` no_road_nearby or no_route. Billed: the route was attempted.

429.description: Per-key rate limit exceeded. Honour Retry-After. Not billed.

get.summary: Whether routing is answering, and the routing limits of each plan

200.description: Routing status, coverage, costs in lookups, and per-plan caps.

snapshot.description: The OpenStreetMap snapshot the routes come from.

get.description:
Returns an API key belonging to one communal account. Its quota, rate limit and single
boundary set are pooled across every anonymous user — fine for evaluation, wrong for
anything real. Create your own key at https://atlasfetch.xyz/dashboard

200.description: The demo key and the public plan's caps.

404.description: No demo key is configured on this deployment.

200.description: Every plan, with prices and caps.

bearerAuth.description:
An API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` — a 64-character hex string with no
prefix. Create one at https://atlasfetch.xyz/dashboard, or call `GET /demo/key` for the
shared public key.

The dashboard endpoints (key management, usage, billing, members) accept only a browser
session, which an automated client cannot obtain, and are not described here.

Error.description: Every 4xx and 5xx body has this shape.

error.description: What went wrong, in a sentence.

code.description: A machine-readable reason, on routing errors.

details.description: Per-field validation problems, when there are any.

ApiError.description: A problem with part of a request that still succeeded.

type.description: `access` — a set was skipped. `usage` — quota exhausted, mirroring a 402.

LayerHit.description: A matched boundary. `null` when that layer matched nothing.

code.description: ISO 3166-1 for country, ISO 3166-2 for region, and for municipal the official ISO code where OpenStreetMap carries one, otherwise a generated `B-<country>-<n>`. Generated codes are not yet stable across a full reseed; ISO codes are.

StreetAnswer.description: The street answer for one radius. A numbered address within the radius wins over a nearer street; for the unlimited radius an address must still be within 20 m. With nothing within the radius, every field but `radiusMeters` is null.

streetNumber.description: A string, not a number: `44A`, `12-14`. Only when an address matched — house numbers are rare.

streetName.description: The street name, or the route number for a road that has only one (`N1`).

postcode.description: A string: some postcodes start with 0. Only when an address matched.

distanceMeters.description: Metres to the building (0 inside it) or to the nearest point of the street, to 0.1 m.

name.description: The boundary name you gave it.

properties.description: Whatever you attached to that boundary.

base.description: One entry per layer named in `base`. A layer that matched nothing is present and null, never absent.

municipal.description: The finest unit available below the region tier — not a consistent kind of thing. Los Angeles returns a city; rural Kansas returns a county. Do not assume it names a city.

street.description: Only when `street` is in `base`. Always three entries, in the order 5 m, 20 m, unlimited. `null` means the point is outside every covered country (see `GET /streets/coverage`), for example at sea; an entry of nulls means covered, but nothing within that radius. No geometry is returned.

sets.description: Keyed by set name; each value is every boundary in that set containing the point.

errors.description: Always present, empty or not. Read it unconditionally.

available.description: The account-wide switch. False on creation.

grantedKeys.description: The API keys allowed to query this set.

BoundarySetCreated.description: Returned by POST /boundaries/sets. Narrower than BoundarySet: a new set has no boundaries and no grants.

PolygonGeometry.description: A single GeoJSON Polygon. MultiPolygon, Feature and FeatureCollection are rejected. Positions are [longitude, latitude] within range. Each ring has at least 4 positions and is closed (last equals first); rings after the first are holes. Self-intersecting polygons are rejected.

BoundaryProperties.description: Flat key/value pairs returned with every match. Keys up to 32 characters; values a string (up to 256 characters), number or boolean. The Public plan (the shared demo key) accepts only category (zone, area, route, place, other), color (green, blue, red, yellow, purple, orange) and priority (low, medium, high).

pointCount.description: Positions across all rings, the number the plan cap counts.

BoundaryWithGeometry.description: One boundary as returned inside GET /boundaries/view.

eviction.description: At the cap: `evict` replaces the oldest, `reject` refuses.

maxWaypoints.description: Locations per route, origin and destination included.

language.description: Instruction language, e.g. en-GB, de-DE, fr-FR.

items.description: 1-32 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter or digit.
1-32 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores, starting with a letter or digit.

vehicle.description: Truck dimensions, only with mode truck.

geometryIndex.description: Span of points in the route line. Only when geometry is returned.

geometry.description: A polyline6 string or a GeoJSON LineString, as requested.

locations.description: Each location as snapped to the road network, and how far it moved.

route.description: The string route, or an index into alternatives.

priceGBP.description: Pence per month. 0 for the free plans.

selfServe.description: Whether it can be bought online.
